en.title: What Should You Do First in a Land Dispute?
en.directAnswer: Start by protecting evidence and identifying the real type of dispute. A land problem may involve ownership, possession, boundary, inheritance, fraud, a forged deed, mortgage or a government record. Do not use force. Collect documents, make a timeline and get the correct legal route for the facts.

atAGlance.whoFor: A citizen has a land conflict and needs safe first steps.

en.lawMeaning:
The 2023 land-crime law contains offences relating to land fraud. A dispute can still be civil, criminal, administrative or a mix, so do not label every land disagreement as a crime.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Photograph current possession and boundaries where safe.
Collect deeds, khatians, maps and mutation papers.
Save tax receipts and payment records.
Check whether forged documents or threats are involved.
Get legal advice before filing the wrong case.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A neighbour moves a boundary marker. Before fighting, the owner saves photos, gets the relevant map and records, and seeks the correct survey/legal remedy.
commonMistakes: filing a criminal complaint only to pressure a civil opponent.
en.specialistTrigger: Threats or violence; forged deed; dispossession; injunction needed; court case; large-value property; unclear title.
en.disclaimer:
This page provides general legal information about Bangladesh. It is not individual legal advice. Laws, procedures, fees and official instructions can change. Check the cited primary sources before taking action.
